headline: Weak eMudhra CA private keys let attackers impersonate websites, browsers respond
summary: Researchers found eMudhra's private keys for eight CA certificates were so weak they could be recovered and used to impersonate any website; major browsers blocked the compromised certificates. eMudhra says it passed audits and calls the issue a minor error, at odds with the severity described elsewhere.

claims.statement: Weak private keys for eight eMudhra CA certificates could let attackers impersonate any website.

sources.quote: Leaked private keys for eight CA certificates let any attacker impersonate any domain
makes it possible to impersonate any website or service

claims.statement: Major browser makers, including Mozilla, Google and Apple, blocked the compromised eMudhra certificates.

sources.quote: Mozilla, Google, Apple block compromised eMudhra CA certificates

claims.statement: eMudhra revoked eight compromised intermediate certificates after researchers found the private keys were easily recoverable.

sources.quote: Certificate authority eMudhra revoked eight compromised intermediate certificates after researchers found their private keys were so weak that anyone could recover them almost instantly

claims.statement: eMudhra said it passed audits and attributed the issue to a minor error.

sources.quote: Says it passed audits and made just a minor mystery error

claims.statement: One of the compromised private keys was reportedly just the number 4.

sources.quote: one of them was the number ‘4’

discrepancies.explanation: eMudhra characterizes the key weakness as a minor error after passing audits, while other coverage describes the flaw as severe enough to let attackers impersonate any domain.
